claims.claim: A modern HTML document uses a doctype declaration before the html element to trigger standards mode.
The html element is the document element and contains head and body in the conventional high-level structure.
The head element collects metadata, while the body element represents the document's content.
A title element supplies a document title and character encoding can be declared with a meta charset element.
Viewport metadata provides viewport-related instructions but does not itself implement a responsive layout.
Browsers have parsing error-recovery behavior, but complete author-written document structure communicates intent more reliably.
